text: Start with opening cash and place expected receipts and payments in the periods when cash actually moves. Include farm sales, seed and other input bills, financing proceeds, capital purchases and debt payments according to their real dates and terms. Carry each period's closing cash into the next to expose temporary deficits; test delayed sale or changed yield scenarios. An annual accrual profit or positive enterprise margin cannot rule out an interim cash shortage. Depreciation changes accounting profit but is not itself a current cash payment, and borrowed principal is financing rather than earned operating revenue. Source basis: Ontario Publication 61 farm planning and USDA ARS WHOLEFARM description. This is a planning structure, not a lender decision.
title: Seasonal farm cash-flow scheduling method

text: Build a crop or livestock enterprise budget for a declared production period, output unit and scale. Estimate revenue from assumed marketable output and price, then name the cost boundary: direct variable cost, broader operating cost, contribution margin or total cost including relevant ownership and shared costs. Keep allocations consistent and avoid double counting. Break-even price or yield divides the chosen cost by the corresponding nonzero output or price on matched units; the answer changes when the cost boundary changes. Replace sample quantities and prices with farm-specific, dated assumptions. Test lower output, lower price and higher cost scenarios, then compare projections with actual records to improve the next budget. Old budget figures are examples, not a current local bid, farm-specific profitability result or permission to sell. Source basis: Manitoba cost guide, Ontario cost-budgeting guide and USDA ARS whole-farm planning description.
title: Enterprise cost-boundary and scenario method

text: Liquidity concerns the ability to meet near-term obligations; solvency describes the balance of debt and asset value. At a dated, consistently valued balance sheet, working capital is current assets minus current liabilities and the current ratio is current assets divided by current liabilities when the denominator is positive. These measures can help describe a cash strain even when land equity is substantial, but neither predicts each payment date or proves profitability, lending approval or a safe investment. Follow with a cash-flow schedule using actual receivable and bill dates. Source basis: USDA ERS ratio definitions and Ontario farm succession financial-ratio guidance; published sector or guide thresholds are not individual-farm diagnoses.
title: Farm liquidity and dated balance-sheet method

text: Before interpreting a nutrient plan, assemble field identity and area, maps and sensitive areas, crop rotation, crop plans and yield records, representative soil and plant tests, manure or amendment analyses, past application history and credible nutrient credits. Track actual and intended source, timing, form, placement and field conditions in records separately from any new calculated rate. An example from another state or province can organize questions but cannot supply this field's nutrient requirement, manure availability, setback, legal duty or application permission. Current local guidance, field samples and applicable rules are required for a prescription or compliant plan. Source basis: USDA NRCS nutrient management planning and Manitoba Agriculture's plan components.
title: Nutrient-plan evidence inventory method

text: Define the proposed change and a consistent comparison period and scale. Record four changes relative to the current practice: added returns, costs avoided, added costs and returns forgone. Net change is added returns plus costs avoided minus added costs minus returns forgone. Count a machinery, labour or ownership item only to the extent it truly changes; do not relabel an unavoidable overhead as a saving. Use farm-specific quotes and records, then vary uncertain yield, timeliness, labour and price assumptions. A positive scenario result is not a guaranteed profit or an approval to implement. Source basis: Iowa State Extension partial budgeting and Ontario Publication 61.
title: Incremental farm-change budget method

text: Choose a crop- and location-appropriate desired established stand separately. For each seed lot, convert that target to seeds to place by accounting for measured germination and an explicit field-establishment assumption; then convert seed count to mass with that lot's seed size or thousand-kernel weight and consistent units. Two lots planted at equal mass can contain different numbers of viable seeds. A laboratory germination result does not guarantee emergence. Calibrate the drill for the selected lot, then record the lot, method, units, setting and subsequent stand count. Source basis: Manitoba Agriculture spring-cereal seeding guidance and Nebraska Extension winter-wheat seed-count guidance. Their crop targets, survival examples and regional tables are not portable recommendations.
title: Seed-count to mass planning method

text: For a declared crop or organism and thermal-time model, convert daily weather to heat units using that model's base temperature, any upper or lower caps, temperature units and accumulation start. A simple daily form uses the nonnegative difference between average daily maximum/minimum temperature and a base; other models use different cutoff rules. Sum only comparable daily values. The resulting accumulation is a development estimate, not an observed crop stage, yield forecast or automatic harvest or treatment trigger. Investigate disagreement with field observations and review moisture, weather inputs and model assumptions without declaring a cause from heat units alone. Source basis: AAFC GDD service and Purdue Extension thermal-time explanation.
title: Thermal-time bookkeeping and interpretation method
